READABILITY.evidence: Names are mostly clear and doc comments are present. But business logic uses single-letter names (`p := &Polygon{}`, `s`, `d`, `e` in decodeShape/decode), and the ~150-line ShapeIndex.decode has almost no inline comments explaining its sections.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: ShapeIndex.decode is about 150 lines, which trips the >100-line cap. Encode/decode went into shapeindex.go instead of a dedicated shapeindex_encode.go. decodeShape handles each type differently (`p.Decode(d.r)`, `p.decode(*d)`, `p.decode(d)`), and the same version/count/vertex boilerplate is copied into every shape.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: In decodeShape, `p.decode(*d); return p, d.err` hands Polyline a copy of the decoder, so a bad version or oversized nvertices sets err on the copy and the outer d.err stays nil. The error is lost on the index-mutation path. Also the magic `maxEdges > 100000`, and a failed decode leaves the index partly filled.

C7-14-CASE1.evidence: Existing tags are untouched and new ones are added as `typeTagLoop = 6` and `typeTagLaxLoop = 7`, below typeTagMinUser. Polygon/Polyline wire formats are unchanged. The Shape interface is not modified, and the new Encode/Decode methods are additive.
